Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

If you're only renewing the signing without changing content, you don't need to rebuild the web artifacts.

If you've modified the blog content, you need to rebuild and sync first:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22.22.2
```

RuokeZhang/pocket48-summarizer.body:
# Pocket48 Replay Summarizer

A web app that can run on your local machine or self-hosted server: paste a link to a public Pocket48 member live share, automatically extract replay audio, generate timestamped subtitles, parse bullet comments, and output a Chinese-language structured summary with subtitle evidence.

Example input:

```text
https://h5.48.cn/2019appshare/memberLiveShare/index.html?id=1297967327104274432
```

## Feature Boundaries

- The main site currently only handles publicly available completed replays that do not require login to access.
- Room members speaking is still an experimental POC with default disabled: the repository provides explicit confirmation for one-time manual SMS login, private account queries, optional 60-second local recording probe, and an independently running capture-first local monitoring process. Monitoring status and safely completed MP3 rolling segments are publicly played and downloaded via `/room-voice`. After recording ends, the existing SQLite Worker automatically discovers sessions, temporarily merges audio, calls DashScope ASR and LLM, and publicly provides read-only subtitles and summaries; simultaneously captures public room text messages within the recording time window, displayed synchronized by time next to the lyrics player. Messages only save public nicknames, text, send time, and relative recording time; they do not save user ID, level, gender, VIP, real name, or credentials. Original segment playback does not depend on successful processing. Monitoring will not automatically resend SMS or perform unattended login retries.
- Does not permanently save raw full-length videos; temporarily extracts audio directly from HLS via FFmpeg.
- Subtitles are generated by a configurable Alibaba Cloud Bailian DashScope non-real-time speech recognition model.
- Summaries are generated through a configurable OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` API.
- SQLite saves tasks, Chinese and English subtitles, translation queues, bullet comments, ASR raw JSON, and summaries.
- After successful recognition, deletes local temporary audio and private OSS temporary objects.
- By default only listens on `127.0.0.1`.
- Can enable invitation accounts: browse completed results publicly, submitting new tasks and editing videos requires login.
- Global deduplication within the same live stream; invitation accounts default to a maximum of 3 task submissions per day.
- Can set `REPLAY_WATCH_MEMBER_ID=407126`, the backend checks Yang Ye's public live broadcast history every 24 hours, automatically processes new replays started after initial enablement. Check time is persisted and restart does not reset the interval; already submitted live streams are not reprocessed, live streams that have not yet generated replays are left for subsequent checking.
- Default no limit on replay duration; to protect resources, you can set a positive number of hours as an upper limit through `MAX_REPLAY_HOURS`, `0` means disabled.
- Timeline clips will first open a desktop popup or mobile fullscreen editor, you can adjust start and end points, snap to subtitles and adjacent silence, click to lock red time markers, and split, delete, or restore segments at markers; preview and export will automatically skip deleted intervals in original order and concatenate all retained segments.

anthonyli/laya-pilot.body:
# LayaPilot · Enterprise-level Admin Backend Automated Testing

[English](https://github.com/anthonyli/laya-pilot/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) · [Local Headless Execution](https://github.com/anthonyli/laya-pilot/blob/HEAD/docs/local-runtime.md) · [Architecture and Extension](https://github.com/anthonyli/laya-pilot/blob/HEAD/docs/architecture.md) · [Roadmap](https://github.com/anthonyli/laya-pilot/blob/HEAD/ROADMAP.md)

Targeting **enterprise-level admin backends**, **generate replayable Excel test cases** from browser pages, or read and execute existing Excel tests. Primarily covers user management, customer management, and other pages centered on tables, filtering, forms, and CRUD operations, with automated accuracy, speed, and stability as the goal, prioritizing local or intranet inference.

The current version uses Playwright to drive the browser and uses local Laya or a compatible decision API to understand fields, select options, and match execution targets. Post-execution assertions are determined by page state, without directly treating model judgment as pass results.

The generation phase retains CRUD templates, with models identifying field purposes, selecting data-filling strategies, and dropdown option categories; options of the same category use stable order selection, with explicit `--data` configuration taking priority. After template completion, the default `discover` operation allows models to select supplementary tests based on current page controls and field constraints: no-result queries, filter resets, cancel additions, email format, numeric bounds. Supplementary tests are only written to Excel after actual execution and assertion passing; replay directly reuses verified steps. Currently bounded candidate decisions that won't automatically infer business rules not declared by the page; entries like approval and import without execution capability will be recorded in the report.

Replay retains test case steps, data, and expected results, with Laya matching clicks, form fills, date and dropdown fields to the current page; even if only one control is found, the decision entry will be called. Identical requests can reuse the model cache from this run; the step stops when the model refuses, confidence is low, or a different value is selected, without unauthorized modification of test cases. Saved text, dates, and dropdown options are executed precisely by original values; pure page assertions don't require the model.

`runs/<this run>/ExecutionResult.xlsx` supports both generation and replay: the generation phase is marked as "Verified on Generation", containing records of success, failure, not applicable, and dependency blocking; replayable test case files still only include verified cases. The `resultFile` in `results.json` points to the result table, and `form-field`, `form-option`, `test-discovery`, `replay-target` in `decisions.ndjson` respectively record field judgment, option selection, supplementary test decisions, and replay target matching. Model loading, actual inference count, and cache hits are respectively counted. …

# Stock Daily Limit Analysis System

## Project Introduction

The Stock Daily Limit Analysis System is a stock data crawling, storage, and analysis platform developed based on the Flask framework. The system is primarily used for crawling stock daily limit data, and provides data query, analysis, and visualization functions to help users better understand the daily limit trends in the stock market.

## Features

### Data Crawling Functions
- Scheduled crawling of daily limit data from stock data APIs
- Support for crawling single-day or historical data by date
- Data deduplication and update mechanisms
- Crawling time restrictions (to avoid interference during trading hours)

### Data Management Functions
- SQLite database storage for stock data
- Table partitioning by date, optimizing query performance
- Automatic index creation to improve search speed
- Support for create, read, update, and delete operations on data

### Search and Filtering Functions
- Stock name keyword search
- Support for Pinyin and Pinyin initial letter search
- Thematic sector filtering
- Date filtering functionality

### Data Visualization Functions
- Stock price increase ranking
- Multi-day board statistics ranking
- Stock candlestick chart display
- Intraday chart data display
- Profit ratio historical data

### System Functions
- Support for scheduled task scheduling (local development environment)
- Vercel deployment support
- Cross-origin request handling
- API request retry mechanism
- Error logging

## Technology Stack

### Backend Technologies
- **Flask**: Python web framework for building APIs and web interfaces
- **SQLite**: Lightweight relational database for storing stock data
- **Requests**: HTTP library for crawling stock data
- **APScheduler**: Scheduled task scheduling library (local development environment)
- **Pypinyin**: Chinese Pinyin conversion library supporting Pinyin search

### Frontend Technologies
- **HTML/CSS**: Building user interfaces
- **JavaScript**: Frontend interaction logic
- **Chart.js**: Chart visualization library

### Deployment Technologies
- **Vercel**: Cloud platform deployment (production environment)
- **GitHub Actions**: CI/CD automation workflow

# DownKyi Core

DownKyi Core is a cross-platform Bilibili video download tool based on the Windows version of DownKyi and Avalonia. The project uses .NET 10, Avalonia 12, Microsoft Generic Host, Microsoft DI, and CommunityToolkit MVVM.

## Download

- Windows: `DownKyi-*-win-x64.zip` or `DownKyi-*-win-x86.zip`
- macOS: `DownKyi-*-osx-arm64.dmg` or `DownKyi-*-osx-x64.dmg`
- Linux: AppImage / deb / rpm

Windows ZIP must be extracted completely to a new directory before running. The `aria2` and `ffmpeg` subdirectories must be retained next to `DownKyi.exe`; if the program reports missing `aria2/aria2c.exe`, please re-download the official Release and extract completely, do not place individual executable files separately.

For version changes, see [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/crazysmile-PhD/downkyicore/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md), and installation packages are available at [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/crazysmile-PhD/downkyicore/releases).

## Features

- Parse video, collection, anime, course, favorites, history, and watch later entries.
- Download audio, video, covers, danmaku, regular subtitles, and AI subtitles.
- Support aria2 and built-in downloader, preserving the state needed for resume.
- When deleting downloading tasks, simultaneously stop the downloader and clean up generated media and temporary files.
- Export diagnostic logs with de-sensitized cookies, tokens, emails, UIDs, and local user paths.

## Running and Data Directory

The release package already includes .NET, FFmpeg, and aria2, no need to install additional runtime environments. FFmpeg prioritizes lossless stream copy; when transcoding is necessary, it detects available hardware encoders, and falls back to software encoding if it fails, recording the reason.

Default data directories:

- Windows: `%APPDATA%\DownKyi`
- macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/DownKyi`
- Linux: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/DownKyi`, usually `~/.config/DownKyi` when not set

Common subdirectories:

- `Media`: Default download directory
- `Logs`: Application and diagnostic logs
- `Storage`: SQLite download database
- `Config`: Settings and login information
- `Cache`: Image and runtime cache
- `Aria`: aria2 session…

# dsh-short-video-studio

**Completely local · Free · Zero cloud dependencies** **short drama / animation canvas studio**, running as a dual-sided plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai). All generation runs on **local ComfyUI** – no need for any paid cloud API, no quota consumption, ready to use out of the box, one generation, unlimited output.

**Image quality can now reach 2K / 4K delivery**: On the generation side, there are **two-stage latent space upscaling** (hires: first pass 896×512 → latent ×1.5 → second pass reconstruction, delivery 1344×768) and **learning-based 3D latent upscaling** (`...-2k` family: ×2 → delivery **2688×1536**); on the post-processing side, there is an independent **video super-resolution** capability `video.upscale` (frame-by-frame CNN ×2 / ×4, **original audio track preserved**) – native clips in one pass ×4 reach **4032×2304** (124 frames tested **241.3s**), or 2K then ×2 to same resolution (**261.6s**). See [Resolution and Image Quality (2K / 4K)](#分辨率与画质2k--4k) for which path to choose.

> In a nutshell: **Agent orchestrates workflows according to the skills you define, dispatches generation requests to local ComfyUI for execution, outputs land in a visual canvas, and you can also remotely control creation through Feishu.**

This plugin is a universal ComfyUI workflow executor + capability registry – **any model that ComfyUI can run** (SDXL / SD3.5 / Qwen-Image / Wan / CogVideoX / LTX / local Kling, etc., images or videos, with or without audio) can be integrated through [importing a workflow manifest](#导入你自己的-comfyui-workflow), with no changes needed to skills and tool contracts. kaloscope/android-tv.body:
# Kaloscope Android TV

> [!WARNING]
> This Android TV client is a Vibe Coding project with code primarily generated with AI assistance.
> Code quality, stability, and device compatibility are not guaranteed. Please evaluate the risks and take responsibility before using.

> [!NOTE]
> This project accepts Pull Requests generated entirely by AI (pure AI PRs).
> Submitters do not need to write code manually, but still need to explain the purpose of changes, complete necessary verification, and take responsibility for their submissions.

This is a native TV client for the [Kaloscope](https://github.com/kaloscope/kaloscope) project, designed for Android TV devices that operate using only remote controls.
The client connects to a server deployed by the user and provides media library browsing, network resource searching, and TV-side video playback, image and text reading capabilities.

This project does not include a server component and does not provide local media management services. Before use, you need to prepare a server that the client can access.

## Features

- Manage multiple servers and save login status separately for each
- Browse recent viewing history, media libraries, media details, and content organized by season and episode
- Search and filter network resources through the server's indexer
- Play local and network videos with support for HLS, DASH, transcoding fallback, and resume playback
- Read images and text resources with support for pagination, zooming, and typography settings
- Player supports chapters, episode selection, subtitles, playback speed, auto-play next, and danmaku

## Installation and Usage

### Requirements

- Android TV device running Android 6.0 (API 23) or higher
- A Kaloscope server accessible to the TV device
- A server account with the required media library or indexer permissions

See the [Deployment Guide](https://kaloscope.org/docs/deployment) for server installation methods.

### Installing APK

1. Go to [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/kaloscope/android-tv/releases) to download the latest APK version.
2. Transfer and install the APK on your Android TV device, and allow the installation as prompted by the system.
3. Open the app, add the server address, and log in to your account.

When installing a new version, you can install it directly over the existing version. Do not uninstall the old version first, to avoid losing locally saved server and login information.

## Project Structure

This project uses a single `app` module, single Activity, and Jetpack Compose UI. The main code is located at `app/src/main/java/org/kaloscope/tv`:


leizongmin/ZeroWeb.body:
# ZeroWeb

ZeroWeb is an experimental cross-platform browser project written in Rust. This repository is doing two things at the same time:

Official Website: [zeroweb.leizm.com](https://zeroweb.leizm.com)

- An embeddable and reusable `ZeroWebView` library
- A complete `ZeroBrowser` browser application

The main project line aims to keep core code and dependency boundaries in its own hands, so the page kernel is gradually built up from Rust components with permissive licenses. DOM, CSS, layout, rendering, navigation, and security boundaries are all being built up layer by layer in this repository.

This is also an AI-first engineering experiment: humans are only responsible for solution design, critical decisions, and result validation, while code development is almost entirely completed autonomously by AI. We want to see how far AI can push such a complex system when architectural boundaries, testing, and acceptance criteria are clearly defined.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This repository is still in the experimental stage and is primarily for learning, research, and engineering exploration. The core crates and tests already have substantial content, but the browser shell, complete JavaScript runtime for pages, and real website compatibility are still in development. It is not currently a daily-use browser. For commercial or other production uses, please evaluate the risks regarding functionality, security, compatibility, performance, and license boundaries on your own.

**Quick Navigation**

- [Roadmap](https://github.com/leizongmin/ZeroWeb/blob/HEAD/ROADMAP.md)

- **Embedding-First**: In addition to the browser application, the project must deliver a stable Rust `ZeroWebView` API to facilitate direct integration by other applications.
- **License Boundaries First**: Mainline dependencies prioritize permissive licenses such as MIT, Apache-2.0, and BSD to avoid core capabilities being constrained by unsuitable copyleft dependencies.
- **Rust Full-Stack Approach**: Page kernel, host layer, and rendering infrastructure are all completed within the Rust ecosystem as much as possible.
- **AI Can Code, But Must Be Reviewable**: AI-assisted contributions are welcome, but submitted changes must be explainable, testable, and comprehensible.

team-framework/innolive-server.body:
# innolive-server

A Go media server that receives real-time WebRTC live broadcasts, processes them through **AI de-identification**, and delivers the processed video to users and broadcasts it to streaming platforms.

The server receives user camera frames and forwards them to an AI server. The AI server blurs faces other than registered faces, and the server delivers the results to users and live. It's a live broadcast server that masks the faces of bystanders visible on the broadcast screen.

---

## Problems This Project Solves

When broadcasting outdoors, faces of people passing behind the broadcaster are visible as-is. innolive-server inserts an AI privacy step in the middle of the broadcast pipeline, keeping only the broadcaster's face and blurring all other faces. If AI processing fails, the server displays a black screen instead of outputting the unprocessed original.

## Key Features

- **WebRTC Ingest/Delivery**: Based on [pion/webrtc](https://github.com/pion/webrtc). Supports STUN/TURN, ICE reconnection grace period, and ICE restart recovery when switching networks.
- **AI Privacy Pipeline**: Sends frames to an AI server to blur faces. Three modes: `bypass`, `fixed_delay`, `real`. Distributes processing across multiple workers using round-robin scheduling.
- **Fail-closed Error Handling**: If AI processing is delayed or fails, outputs a black screen instead of the unprocessed original.
- **AI Worker Continuous Monitoring**: Periodically runs probes that round-trip actual frames to detect workers where the process is alive but inference is dead.
- **Platform Broadcasting**: Creates broadcasts on YouTube accounts connected by users and outputs via RTMP using FFmpeg. Separates broadcast preparation and live transition to allow screen preview before viewer visibility.
- **Broadcast Settings Storage**: Stores title, description, visibility, kid-friendly status, category, and thumbnail in the session and applies them during broadcast preparation.
- **De-identification Toggle**: Turns AI processing on and off while maintaining the broadcast.
- **Reference Face Management**: Registers and deletes "own face" to be excluded from blurring via REST API.
- **Session Ownership Authentication**: Issues per-session tokens so only owners can control sessions.
- **User Account Management**: PostgreSQL + GORM.…

| `url` | Yes | File address, supports OFD, PDF |
| `name` | No | File name, automatically obtained by default |
| `page` | No | Physical page number, default 1, if exceeded, take the last page |

Parameters are connected with `&`, parameter values require URL encoding. For cross-origin access, the server header must include:

```http
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://ofdgo.aite.me
```

xxxzhou/avox.description: Cross-platform media SDK (C++17): capture / GPU pipeline / player / record. Successor of aoce.
xxxzhou/avox.body:
# avox

avox is a cross-platform audio-video capability library (C++17) that provides a unified pipeline from device capture, hardware decode/encode, GPU image processing to rendering, streaming and recording. The player is currently the most complete module; WebRTC real-time communication and AI capabilities (speech recognition, machine translation, image restoration, super-resolution) are integrated on-demand in plugin form; XR/VR·MR camera calibration and virtual-real fusion (virtual production) modules have been verified in production and integrated, with virtual human (digital human) modules currently being integrated; texture-level direct passthrough has been achieved with UE5, Unity3D, and Godot game engines.

avox is derived from the author's years of accumulated audio-video/GPU technology expertise, organized with the assistance of large models. The technical lineage extends from the early [OEIP](https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/104027165) (UE4/Unity3D multimedia pipeline) to [aoce](https://github.com/xxxzhou/aoce) (Vulkan cross-platform GPU image processing), with key implementation processes documented as a series of technical articles ([Tian Tian Bu Zai](https://www.zhihu.com/people/zhou-xin-12-70-21/posts)), see the [Technical Implementation Analysis](#技术实现解析) section below.

## Project Advantages

- **One codebase, multiple platforms** - Windows / Android / iOS / Linux single C++17 codebase, unified CMake build; platform differences in hardware decode/encode, GPU interoperability, window systems, etc. are abstracted at the framework layer, extending to new platforms requires only implementing the platform layer interface
- **Single interface definition, four-language bindings with zero manual effort** - Export layer is pure virtual abstract interface + `create*` factory + `addXxxOb/removeXxxOb` callback registration, STL types disabled (`const char*`, naked pointers + ref counting, callback classes), SWIG automatically generates C# / Java / Node.js / Python bindings from the same header files; callback classes can be directly inherited and overridden in each language through the director mechanism, new interfaces require no per-language binding layer maintenance
- **Full-path GPU zero-copy** - Hardware decode (DX11VA/MediaCodec/VideoToolbox) → Vulkan image processing → hardware encode/rendering, data stays on GPU throughout without CPU transfer.
  - **Windows** - D3D11VA hardware decode frames as DX11 textures via shared handle with Vulkan interoperability directly into the processing pipeline, results back to DX11/DX12/Vulkan rendering to window; MF camera, screen capture connected via unified data source interface
  - **Android** - NdkCamera2 camera OES texture direct output, cross-EGLContext interoperability with Vulkan, MediaCodec hardware decode output AHardwareBuffer directly into pipeline, results back to OpenGL ES/Vulkan rendering to Surface or via MediaCodec GPU…
